blocks.content: The survey builder takes a {{term:customer-survey|customer survey}} from draft to evaluation without the data ever leaving the project: build the questionnaire, send it as a self-contained HTML file, import the returned answer files and evaluate them.

Recipients need nothing but a browser. The HTML file works offline and without installation; at the end it saves a small JSON file with the answers, which comes back by e-mail. There is no server and no online return channel.
Create the header, sections and questions, set conditions and click through the questionnaire in the preview. "Export questionnaire" creates the general file without a recipient.
Create one HTML file per recipient. The list shows who received which version and who has already answered.
Import answer files, evaluate each question, filter, group by a single-choice question and export a report. Free texts go to the {{term:voc|VoC}} tree, Kano questions to the Kano module.

First settle the question the survey has to answer, then pick the question types: single and multiple choice for classification, the rating matrix (1 to 5) for satisfaction, the Kano question for requirements following the {{term:kano-fragebogen|Kano questionnaire}}, free text for everything that cannot be foreseen.

A single-choice question about the customer group at the start pays off twice: through conditions it controls which sections someone sees, and later it is the basis of the group comparison. Conditions always refer to answers further up; hidden questions are never required.

After the first send, every structural change counts as a new version. Recipients holding an older version are marked in the list and can receive a new file; their answers are still imported, and answers that no longer match a question are dropped.

In the evaluation, filtering comes first, then grouping. Group values that deviate from the overall mean by at least 0.5 are highlighted; groups with fewer than five responses carry the note "few responses". The hand-over to the Kano module always takes all responses, regardless of the filter.
Three responses per group show a direction, not proof. The group comparison computes no significance; the "few responses" note is meant seriously.
Deleting options or changing a question type once answers have arrived loses the matching answers. Adding new questions and options is harmless.
"Evaluate anonymously" hides names in the evaluation and in the report. The recipient list itself stays, so the response rate remains visible.
Wording such as "How much do you value our fast support?" dictates the answer. Ask neutrally and leave the judgement to the scale.
